rows.text: Korvold draws a card for EVERY permanent you sacrifice, not just the one his own trigger demands. That is the deck. Give him a free sacrifice outlet and a supply of tokens and he turns a board of Treasures into a hand of cards and a 20/20 body at the same time. Note his attack trigger is mandatory — "sacrifice another permanent" — so always have fodder available before you swing, or you will be eating your own mana rocks.

guide.title: The commander and the free outlets

rows.name: Korvold, Fae-Cursed King
rows.text: a counter and a card on every sacrifice, from any source. Five mana, flies, and grows out of removal range within a turn.

rows.name: Ashnod's Altar
rows.text: free, repeatable, and it makes mana. Every creature is two colourless and a card.

rows.name: Phyrexian Altar
rows.text: the same with colour fixing, which matters in three colours.

rows.name: Goblin Bombardment
rows.text: free, and it converts the fodder into reach at the face.

rows.name: Skullclamp
rows.text: on a 1/1 token, two cards — plus Korvold's card for the death. Three cards per token.

rows.name: Deadly Dispute
rows.text: two cards and a Treasure for a spare artifact or creature, at instant speed.

rows.name: Diabolic Intent
rows.text: a tutor for a spare body, and Korvold draws off the sacrifice.

rows.name: Baba Lysaga, Night Witch
rows.text: sacrifice three permanents of three different types for three drain, three life and three cards — plus three Korvold triggers.

rows.name: Academy Manufactor
rows.text: every Treasure you would make becomes a Clue, a Food AND a Treasure. It triples every token maker below and turns each one into three Korvold draws when they get sacrificed.

rows.name: Pitiless Plunderer
rows.text: a Treasure for every creature that dies. With an Altar out this is how a board unravels into a dozen cards.

rows.name: Grim Hireling
rows.text: two Treasures per combat damage step.

rows.name: Professional Face-Breaker
rows.text: a Treasure per combat step, and it converts Treasures into impulse draws.

rows.name: Goldspan Dragon
rows.text: Treasures on attack and whenever anyone targets it, and your Treasures tap for two mana instead of one.

rows.name: Impulsive Pilferer
rows.text: a Treasure when it dies, and encore makes three more copies later.

rows.name: Jadar, Ghoulcaller of Nephalia
rows.text: a free 2/2 every single end step, forever. It is the most reliable fodder in the deck.

rows.name: Ophiomancer
rows.text: a 1/1 deathtouch Snake every upkeep, which blocks anything and then becomes a card.

rows.name: Marionette Apprentice
rows.text: fabricate gives you a Servo, and every artifact or creature that dies drains the table.

rows.name: Sakura-Tribe Elder
rows.text: a land and a card in one body.

rows.name: Black Market Connections
rows.text: a Treasure, a card and a 3/2 every turn, for life.

rows.name: The Gitrog Monster
rows.text: an extra land drop, and a card for every land that reaches your graveyard — stacking with Korvold's card for the sacrifice. His upkeep cost is not a drawback here, it is a second trigger.

rows.name: Crucible of Worlds
rows.text: play those lands back out of the graveyard.

rows.name: Ramunap Excavator
rows.text: the creature version, and it is a Snake for Ophiomancer.

rows.name: Sylvan Safekeeper
rows.text: sacrifice lands for free to protect Korvold. Each one is a Korvold card and a Gitrog card, so the "cost" is card advantage.

rows.name: Aftermath Analyst
rows.text: mills three, then sacrifices itself to return EVERY land from your graveyard to the battlefield at once. With Lotus Cobra out that is a huge mana turn; with Korvold it is one card.

rows.name: Lotus Cobra
rows.text: mana on every landfall, which the Analyst turn multiplies.

rows.name: Six
rows.text: mills on attack, keeps a land, and lets you recast permanents from the graveyard by discarding lands.

rows.name: Blood Artist
rows.text: a drain for every creature that dies, anywhere.

rows.name: Cauldron of Essence
rows.text: the same drain, plus a reanimation outlet.

rows.name: Marionette Apprentice
rows.text: a drain for every artifact or creature you lose, which includes every Treasure you crack.

rows.name: Mirkwood Bats
rows.text: a drain when you CREATE a token and again when you sacrifice it. With Academy Manufactor that is six drains per Treasure trigger.

rows.name: Mayhem Devil
rows.text: a damage every time ANY player sacrifices anything — including their own fetchlands.

rows.name: Juri, Master of the Revue
rows.text: grows on every sacrifice and throws all of it at a face when he dies.

rows.name: Chandra's Ignition
rows.text: point it at Korvold. His power hits every other creature on the board and every opponent in the face. This is the deck's cleanest kill.

rows.name: Bolas's Citadel
rows.text: cast off the top paying life, then sacrifice ten nonland permanents for ten damage to each opponent. In a deck making three tokens per trigger, ten permanents is one turn's work.

rows.name: Reanimate
rows.text: one mana for whatever you sacrificed.

rows.name: Living Death
rows.text: your graveyard is deeper than theirs after two turns of this.

rows.name: Eternal Witness
rows.text: any card back, and it is a body to sacrifice afterwards.

rows.name: Cauldron of Essence
rows.text: a repeatable reanimation each turn.

rows.name: Assassin's Trophy
rows.text: two mana for any permanent.

rows.name: Abrupt Decay
rows.text: uncounterable, and most problem permanents cost three or less.

rows.name: Chaos Warp
rows.text: the answer to an enchantment or planeswalker.

rows.name: Blasphemous Act
rows.text: cheap, and this deck profits from its own creatures dying.

rows.name: Heroic Intervention
rows.text: hexproof and indestructible through a wrath.

rows.name: Sylvan Safekeeper
rows.text: shroud on Korvold for a land you did not need.

rows.name: Lightning Greaves
rows.text: haste so he attacks immediately, and shroud against the removal spell.

rows.name: Deflecting Swat
rows.text: free with your commander out.

rows.name: Braids, Arisen Nightmare
rows.text: every end step, you feed it a token and they either give up a permanent or you draw and they lose two.

rows.name: Birds of Paradise
rows.text: turn-one fixing.

rows.name: Ignoble Hierarch
rows.text: all three colours plus exalted.

rows.name: Delighted Halfling
rows.text: uncounterable mana for Korvold himself.

rows.name: Deathrite Shaman
rows.text: mana, drain and lifegain from a one-drop.

rows.name: Nature's Lore
rows.text: an untapped dual with a basic type.

rows.name: Farseek
rows.text: the same for shocklands.

rows.name: Demonic Tutor
rows.text: any card.

rows.name: Diabolic Intent
rows.text: any card for a token you were going to sacrifice anyway.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep mana and a token maker. Jadar, Ophiomancer or a Treasure source means Korvold's attack trigger never costs you anything real, and that is what lets him attack every turn.
Never attack without spare fodder. Korvold's sacrifice on attack is not optional. Sacrificing a Signet or a land to swing for four is usually a worse deal than not attacking at all.

rows.name: Academy Manufactor
rows.text: this is the biggest single multiplier in the deck. Every Treasure effect becomes three tokens, so every drain payoff, every Mirkwood Bats trigger and every Korvold draw triples.

rows.name: Chandra's Ignition
rows.text: hold it until Korvold is at eight power or more. It kills the table's board and usually two players at once, and it does not care about blockers.
